scoring.grading: ambiguous rows excluded from headline, reported separately
scoring.primary_tokens: surface form calibrated per model against a forward pass; *_agg sums variants, evaluation-only

prompts.eligibility:
You are screening a patient for a clinical trial.
Inclusion: <inclusion_rule>.
Patient: <patient_detail>
Is the patient eligible for the trial? Answer Yes or No.
prompts.grading:
You are assessing a patient for a clinical trial.
Patient: <patient_detail>
What is the patient's ECOG performance status grade? Answer with a single digit: 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

rows.patient: Fully active, able to carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction
rows.notes: anchor case - ECOG 0 definition verbatim

rows.patient: Restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature, e.g. light house work, office work
rows.notes: anchor case - ECOG 1 definition verbatim; upper edge of inclusion

rows.patient: Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities; up and about more than 50% of waking hours
rows.notes: anchor case - ECOG 2 definition verbatim; lower edge of exclusion

rows.patient: Patient walking and working normally
rows.notes: paraphrase set S01

rows.patient: Back at the office full time and running again on weekends
rows.notes: same patient as E004 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Patient working at office but no strenuous activity
rows.notes: paraphrase set S02

rows.patient: Doing desk work most days. Gave up the gym but manages the stairs at home fine
rows.notes: same patient as E006 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Patient able to walk unassisted but not able to work
rows.notes: the decisive case - 1/2 boundary is light work vs unable to work

rows.patient: Gets around the house on her own and does her own washing. Had to stop work entirely - cannot manage a shift
rows.notes: same patient as E008 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Ambulatory and self-caring but out of work; resting for roughly half the day
rows.notes: paraphrase set S04

rows.patient: Up and dressed most of the day though he naps after lunch. Not been in to work since March. Manages showering and meals himself
rows.notes: same patient as E010 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Capable of only limited self-care; confined to bed or chair more than half of waking hours
rows.notes: ECOG 3 definition verbatim

rows.patient: Needs help washing and dressing. Spends most of the day in the recliner
rows.notes: same patient as E012 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Patient unable to lift heavy weights but otherwise at baseline
rows.notes: contestable 0 vs 1; grade ambiguous while eligibility is not

rows.patient: Reports feeling exhausted and low but continues full time work and all usual activities
rows.notes: sounds unwell but activity is unrestricted; ECOG is defined by function not distress

rows.patient: Looks well and denies symptoms. Retired last year and has not worked since; independent for all self-care and out most of the day
rows.notes: not working for non-clinical reasons - employment status is not the criterion

rows.patient: Walks the dog each morning without difficulty. Stopped teaching because she could not get through a full day
rows.notes: opens with a healthy-sounding cue but work capacity is lost

rows.patient: Uses a stick outdoors after a knee replacement three years ago. Works full time with no restriction
rows.notes: walking aid predates and is unrelated to the disease under study

rows.patient: Fully back to her usual routine, no restrictions on activity
rows.notes: paraphrase set S06

rows.patient: Training for a 10k again and put in a full week at the shop with no trouble
rows.notes: same patient as E019 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Cleared for light duties only; no heavy lifting or long shifts, but attending work daily
rows.notes: paraphrase set S07

rows.patient: Back on the shop floor doing stock-taking and paperwork; the warehouse team covers anything that means lifting or long hours
rows.notes: same patient as E021 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Managing part-time consulting work from home, skips anything physically demanding
rows.notes: paraphrase set S08

rows.patient: Still billing hours most weeks, just turns down travel and anything that keeps her on her feet all day
rows.notes: same patient as E023 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Left her job to care for her husband after his surgery; still walks daily, cooks, and could return to light duties if needed
rows.notes: second instance of the not-working trap; caregiving is a non-clinical reason for work status

rows.criterion_text: ECOG >= 2 required for enrollment (supportive care cohort)
rows.patient: Restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature
rows.notes: same functional picture as the ECOG 1 anchor definition, protocol flipped; tests whether the model reads the criterion or pattern-matches ECOG <= 1 as standard

rows.patient: Up and independent for all self-care, but had to close her tutoring business entirely
rows.notes: paraphrase set S09

rows.patient: Gets herself ready and manages the house fine, but hasn't been able to take on students since the spring - can't get through a session
rows.notes: same patient as E027 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Independent with all personal care; resting on the sofa most afternoons and no longer able to do his consulting calls
rows.notes: paraphrase set S10

rows.patient: Dresses and feeds himself without help. Cancelled every client meeting since March - can't hold a conversation that long without needing to lie down
rows.notes: same patient as E029 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Patient's NYHA functional class is II. She is independent in all self-care but has been unable to return to her job as a cashier since starting treatment
rows.notes: plants an NYHA value in an oncology vignette; correct ECOG answer depends on the described function, not the other scale's label

rows.patient: Before starting chemotherapy she was working full-time without limitation; three cycles in, she is independent for self-care but has not been able to work since
rows.notes: two time points in one vignette (pre-treatment vs current); tests whether the model selects current status rather than baseline

rows.patient: Needs help from his wife to bathe and dress; spends most of the day lying down
rows.notes: paraphrase set S11

rows.patient: His wife has taken over his showers and getting him into clean clothes; he's in the recliner more than he's out of it
rows.notes: same patient as E033 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Spends most of the day in bed since the fevers started; family manages her meals and washing now
rows.notes: standalone grade 3 case for volume; not part of a matched set

rows.patient: Completely disabled; cannot carry on any self-care; totally confined to bed or chair
rows.notes: ECOG 4 definition verbatim - anchor case, closes the grade-4 warning

rows.patient: Bedbound and reliant on caregivers for all daily needs
rows.notes: paraphrase set S12

rows.patient: Hasn't left the bed in weeks; his son handles feeding, bathing, everything
rows.notes: same patient as E037 - lexically distant restatement

rows.patient: Unable to sit up without assistance; nursing staff provide all care around the clock
rows.notes: standalone grade 4 case for volume; not part of a matched set
